Duration::argsort¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Series Duration::argsort() const;

Return The Ordering, Not The Values¶

argsort() returns the zero-based source positions that would arrange a one-dimensional Duration in ascending elapsed-time order. The returned object is an Int64 Series, because its lanes are positions rather than elapsed values.

Ordering is stable. Equal finite values retain their source order, all NaT lanes follow finite values, and multiple NaT lanes also retain source order. These guarantees make the result suitable for applying the same permutation to associated arrays.

The receiver must be rank one. A scalar or N-D receiver is rejected rather than implicitly flattened, because flattening would erase the structural meaning of the returned positions. Empty rank-one input is valid and returns an empty rank-one Int64 Series.

Examples¶

Example 1. Read the stable permutation, including duplicate and NaT positions.

auto values = pluss::duration::nanos(
    {3, pluss::Duration::kNaT, 1, 3, pluss::Duration::kNaT, 2});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(values.argsort());

Output¶

Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[2, 5, 0, 3, 1, 4]

Positions 0 and 3 both contain three, so stability keeps 0 first. The two absent lanes similarly remain in source order at the end.

Example 2. Apply the positions at an explicit host boundary.

auto order = values.argsort().to_vec<std::int64_t>();
auto source = values.host();
std::vector<std::int64_t> arranged;
arranged.reserve(order.size());
for (auto i : order) arranged.push_back(source[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)]);

std::cout << pluss::duration::print(pluss::duration::nanos(arranged));

Output¶

Duration(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6)
[ 0 days 00:00:00.000000001, 0 days 00:00:00.000000002, 0 days 00:00:00.000000003, 0 days 00:00:00.000000003, NaT, NaT ]

Example 3. Empty is valid; rank two is not.

auto empty = pluss::duration::nanos(std::vector<std::int64_t>{});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(empty.argsort()); // shape [0]

pluss::duration::nanos({1,2,3,4}, {2,2}).argsort();
// throws: Duration::argsort requires rank-one input

See Also¶

  • sort(): return the arranged durations directly.

  • unique(): retain first occurrences without sorting.
